correctness.rationale: For any positive infected-cat equilibrium, the O and I equations force O=kI/mu0 and S=(alpha-mu*t1)*mu0/(beta*k), the mouse equation forces M=0, and the S equation uniquely forces I. Exact signs of I and V=1-S-I establish the two sharp beta thresholds; the flux on V=0 proves the sharp simplex-invariance condition. Strict inequalities, endpoints, effective removal and H positivity are checked. The included standalone rational verifier runs successfully on actual package content; it is not substituted for the symbolic argument.

value.rationale: Physical feasibility of epidemiological equilibria requires nonnegative susceptible, infected and vaccinated/recovered fractions. In a naturally motivated congenital-recruitment regime admitted by the model, the conventional one-sided R0 threshold is insufficient and there is a sharp nontrivial upper transmission cutoff distinct from the invasion threshold. The theorem also fully classifies when the normalized cat simplex is a valid dynamical state region. These exact structural conditions alter interpretation of a published existence/well-posedness claim; they are not arbitrary numerical slices, mere renaming, or a minor type check.
